On the other hand, using the sum of two columns of Y as r can save the factor of log n in the requirement on θ since the “collision” of non-zero entries in the two columns of X creates a larger gap between |b|(1) and |b|(2) . The algorithm using a single column exploited the fact that there exists a reasonable gap between |b|(1) and |b|(2) , whereas the two-column variant ER-SpUD(DC) succeeds even if the nonzeros all have the same magnitude.
